The neighbourhood is bounded on the west by the railroad Amsterdam - Hilversum (with the Muiderpoort Station), on the east side by Flevopark, on the north side by Zeeburgerdijk and on the south side by the Ringvaart Watergraafsmeer. neighborhood_overview:
The Nieuwmarkt-area is one of the oldest in Amsterdam, where Jewish and Chinese cultures left their cultural marks and where commerce thrived, symbolised by the former castle-like weighing station of 'De Waag', right in its centre. There are markets and activities almost every day. The area offers a lot of cafés and restaurants. On the west side you'll find the old seamen's area 'De Wallen', better known as the 'Red Light District', on the east side are the small and quiet streets of the 'Lastage' area, home to shipping warfs and warehouses centuries ago.

The Spaarndammerbuurt is a part of the district Amsterdam West. The area is named after the Spaarndammerdijk and – street, which accumulates the northern and eastern boundary.

The construction of the Spaarndammerbuurt started at the end of the 19th century. The streets have been named after places situated in the West and northwest of Amsterdam. The labor houses had especially been intended for the dock workers, who worked in the ports nearby.

The most famous buildings in the Spaarndammerbuurt are designed by Michel de Klerk, who devised labor apartments in the style of the Amsterdam School, situated at the Spaarndammerplantsoen. In the years around 1920, three of his housing blocks got constructed.

The most striking design is 'The Ship’, located along the Zaanstraat. The houses were 'palaces for the workers’, because before no one really cared about the design of the worker’s houses.

neighborhood_overview:
Oud-West is a neighborhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands, roughly covering the area between the Overtoom, a major thoroughfare west of the city centre, and the parallel De Clercqstraat, a shopping street. The neighbourhood consists of two historically and demographically distinct communities: the Overtoombuurt in the south and the Kinkerbuurt in the north.
Oud-West was a separate borough of Amsterdam until the 2010 borough reforms, when it merged with the boroughs of Bos en Lommer, De Baarsjes and Westerpark to form the larger borough of Amsterdam-West.
Main shopping areas are the Kinkerstraat, De Clercqstraat, Jan Pieter Heijestraat, Overtoom, and Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. Oud-West is served by tram routes 1, 7 and 17 connecting the centre of the city with the western suburbs via the Overtoom (route 1) and Kinkerstraat (routes 7 and 17), as well as routes 3 and 12 running along the Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat.

The neighborhood, known locally by the moniker the "Fred", is centered on the Frederik Hendrikplantsoen park and was planned during the last quarter of the nineteenth century as a confluence of green space and housing meant to be stand apart from the overcrowded Jordaan district. The construction of the neighborhood was mostly complete by the start of the Second World War (1940).

neighborhood_overview:
The house can be found on Realeneiland, a small island that is part of the city centre of Amsterdam, but slightly hidden away from the rest. The realeneiland is part of a group of three islands that together are called 'The Western Isles' (Westelijke eilanden), the two other isles being Bickerseiland and Prinseneiland.

The Western Isles are among the oldest areas of Amsterdam and have a rich history. The house itself is actually one of the fourteen original 'captain's houses' (kapiteinswoningen) of Realeneiland.

The house carries the name 'In 't Anker', which translates as 'in the anchor'; the name along with the house's symbol can be seen on the gable. It can be found on the Zandhoek - the name for the street and corner of the island. As you walk around the neighbourhood you will see boats everywhere, as the island also functions as a small city harbour.

Lose yourself for hours in Amsterdam’s extremely instagrammable and lively Latin Quarter, with its colourful mix of cuisines, terraces and convivial cafés. From the beautiful landscaped gardens of Sarphatipark to the famous Albert Cuypmarkt street market, De Pijp oozes beatnik flair from every angle, and has been a popular haunt for creatives, students and bohemian spirits since the 60s.

The most famous and busiest street market of the Netherlands, the Albert Cuyp Market, is in De Pijp. It is open six days per week and attracts many tourists. The former Heineken brewery is also a popular tourist attraction. Next to the former Heineken brewery is the Marie Heinekenplein, which has a number of bars and cafes. neighborhood_overview:
Amsterdam Canal District is a neighborhood in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The seventeenth-century canals in Amsterdam, located in the center of Amsterdam, were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in August 2010. The Amsterdam Canal District consists of the area around the city's four main canals: Singel, Herengracht, Keizersgracht and Prinsengracht. From Brouwersgracht, the canals are generally parallel to each other, and gradually lead southeast into the Amstel River.

Many of the canal houses in the Amsterdam Canal District are from the Dutch Golden Age in the 18th century. However, many of these buildings underwent restoration or reconstruction in different centuries, which means that these buildings display many different architectural styles and facades.

neighborhood_overview:
When strolling around the dainty, crooked streets of the Jordaan today, it’s difficult to comprehend that the neighbourhood used to be a pit of poverty on the verge of demolition. Constructed in the early 17th century, when Amsterdam’s first Golden Age saw a steady influx of wealthy European immigrants, the Jordaan was originally dubbed the Nieuwe Werck (‘New Work’), as it housed the working-class artisans, carpenters and masons toiling away to expand the city’s boundaries. It even became Rembrandt’s last home following his bankruptcy in 1655.

Today, the Jordaan offers a real mix: old-fashioned community-oriented Jordanese residents live next door to well-to-do young families shuttling their kids to school in a bakfiets (cargo bicycle). There are numerous hip hangouts and trendy restaurants around Noordermarkt and along Westerstraat and Rozengracht, but there’s also no shortage of traditional brown cafés. Rivierenbuurt is a neighbourhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands. The neighbourhood is situated in the eastern part of the borough of Amsterdam-Zuid, bordered by the river Amstel to the east, the Boerenwetering canal in the west, the Amstelkanaal in the north and the A10 motorway in the south. In 2013, the Rivierenbuurt had approximately 28,400 residents.[1]

The Dutch word Rivierenbuurt translates as 'Rivers Neighbourhood', which refers to the fact that most streets in the area are named after rivers in the Netherlands.

neighborhood_overview:
Our apartment is located in one of the most popular areas of Amsterdam called 'Rivierenbuurt'/'De Pijp'. Rivierenbuurt literally translates to ‘River neighborhood’. It's name stems from the fact that most of the streets here are named after rivers in the Netherlands. This residential neighborhood was developed in the 1920s for Amsterdam’s middle class. It was part of architect Hendrik Petrus Berlage's ‘Plan Zuid’, and was considered quite an architectural wonder in those days. Even today, architecture buffs find their way around the many examples of Amsterdam School architecture.

De Pijp is one of Amsterdam's most popular neighborhoods. Lose yourself for hours in this lively Latin Quarter of Amsterdam, with its colorful mix of cuisines, terraces and convivial cafes. name: Jordaan Loft apartment
description: Unique loft apartment situated in the center of Amsterdam, in the renowned Jordaan area. This 92m2 apartment (1000sq.ft) has a rooftop terrace and a balcony facing the south-west with views of the courtyard and the beautiful Westerkerk (church). The apartment was built in 1996 in authentic Amsterdam style; meaning you have the comforts of a modern apartment but the charm of a traditional Amsterdam canalhouse.
neighborhood_overview:
Originally a working-class neighbourhood, the Jordaan has become one of the most upscale locations in the Netherlands. It is home to many art galleries, particularly for modern art, and is also dotted with speciality shops and restaurants. Markets are held regularly at Noordermarkt, the Westerstraat (the Lapjesmarkt textile market) and Lindengracht.

Rembrandt spent the last years of his life in the Jordaan, on the Rozengracht canal. He was buried in the Westerkerk church, at the corner of Rozengracht and Prinsengracht, just beyond the Jordaan. The Anne Frank House, where Anne Frank went into hiding during World War II, is located on the edge of the Jordaan, on the Prinsengracht canal.

description: If you are looking for a hotel room with a view in Amsterdam, this is it! Consisting of multiple artificial islands that are connected by bridges over canals, the city’s most recent expansion area ‘IJburg’ still feels like the real Amsterdam. Presumably because of its amazing views – especially during sunrise and sunset – the neighbourhood is rapidly growing more popular and numerous trendy boutiques, classy restaurants and stylish clubs set up shop here, many of them attracting residents from all over Amsterdam. All in all there’s much to do on the island itself, but if you feel like visiting other areas in Amsterdam, tram 26 takes you directly to Amsterdam Central Station in about 30 minutes.

This bridge house is classed as NOISE LEVEL - LOW.

neighborhood_overview:
The northern part of Amsterdam is hip and up-and-coming. Lots of parks and attractions like the Eye film museum and Amsterdam Tower across the water from Central Station.
The part we live in is known in Dutch as a 'Tuindorp' - literally a garden village. A lot of these garden villages were built around Amsterdam in the 1930s to get labourers and their families out of the city slums into decent living conditions with a garden.

The North-South metro line that took 20 years to build opened in July 2018 and runs from the north (8-minute walk from the house) right to the south of the city in 15 minutes. The project overran the budget massively. They say that every second of the 15-minute trip cost 3 million euros to build - so make sure you enjoy the ride!!
If you want to shop for food, there's a little grocery store 5 minutes' walk away and big supermarkets like Lidl and Jumbo 1 km away.

neighborhood_overview: De Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid maakt deel uit van Plan Zuid van H.P. Berlage. Plan Zuid valt uiteen in verschillende delen: de Apollobuurt en Stadionbuurt, gericht op welgestelden, middenklasse en arbeidersklasse, en de Rivierenbuurt, gericht op de middenklasse. De Rivierenbuurt is gebouwd in de jaren twintig en dertig van de 20e eeuw. From this unique hotel room in Amsterdam Centre, perched high above the water, you can see how centuries of development made this city into the miraculous place it is now.

neighborhood_overview:
Many Amsterdam icons can be seen from the panoramic bedroom: the Schreierstoren (built in 1487) reminds us of the old defensive wall that used to stand here, the Maritime Museum with its VOC ship ‘De Amsterdam’ takes us back to the Dutch Golden Age, and the modern science museum NEMO shows us the history of knowledge. No wonder that architecture centre ARCAM is situated right next to the bridge house: this place is a goldmine for architectural history!

The central location of bridge house Kortjewantsbrug is the ideal starting point for any hot spots and must-sees in Amsterdam Center and beyond. Check out our self-composed Neighbourhood Guide on the tablet in the room for recommendations!

Enjoy a ride on the free ferry which will take you to Amsterdam Central Station within 15 minutes.
The neighborhood is also near a wonderful nature parc.

We love the North part of Amsterdam because there is so much to do and to see. The industrial, cosmopolitan feel of the wharf, the cute village houses, loads of bars and great (!!) places to eat. There is a huge flea market and several fresh produce markets. And not to mention a wonderful nature parc (the Twiske) just a bicycle ride away.
Within 15 minutes the free ferry will take you to central station to enjoy the canals, the museum district or many other wonderful area's of town.

neighborhood_overview:
The Jordaan is possibly the most famous neighbourhood in the Netherlands. Akin to the reputation enjoyed by London’s Cockneys, this once working-class bastion was renowned for tight community bonds, radical politics and a love for drink and over-the-top sing-a-longs. Gentrification of decades past has attracted more galleries, restaurants, specialty shops and upwardly-mobile residents to its scenic streets but there’s undeniably still a distinct atmosphere to be enjoyed here.

The Jordaan begins at Brouwersgracht, just west of the Amsterdam Central Station and arches around the western side of Canal Ring between Prinsengracht and Lijnbaansgracht before ending at Leidsegracht. The area north of Rozengracht is a more ‘touristy’ and commercial section, although the quieter area to the south is no less scenic.

De Pijp is a charming, bohemian neighbourhood in Amsterdam, outside the central canal rings, and neighbouring the famous Museumplein (museum square).

It’s where the locals hang & reside, away from the busy tourist centre. It holds a lively yet welcoming character given the multitude of markets, shops and restaurants.

Streets in this neighbourhood are very green, with plants growing from every sidewalk “garden” or pots covering entire street corners.

If you want to truly experience Amsterdam from a local’s perspective, this is the place for you.

name: Lovely 1 bedroom apartment in Amsterdam
description:
This apartment is perfect for your stay in Amsterdam. It's large, bright, and has a really nice balcony that has morning/afternoon sun where you can sit and relax. It has a very spacious living room dining area, and a large bedroom.

It's very well connected to central Amsterdam via the metro and trains from the nearby Bijlmer station. You can also rent bikes from local shops to make your way around.

neighborhood_overview:
This neighbourhood is amazing and very vibrant. Right downstairs from the building you will find the Amsterdamse Poort with plenty of shops. You have Lidl, Albert Heijn and Vomar (for groceries), but also a local market twice a week and plenty of local stores selling groceries.

In addition you will find all sorts of other shops (H&M, Blokker) and restaurants, from cafes to KFC and McDonalds, or Asian takeaway.

It's right next door to the Bijlmer station which also means access to the football stadium and arena for concerts, and a cinema complex with IMax. There is also a gym and a crossfit centre nearby. Of course, you are also well connected to Amsterdam centre by public transport.

If you want to relax, right next door is the gigantic Nelson Mandela park with loads of open space.

name: Gorgeous canal boat with rooftop terrace in centre
neighborhood_overview: The boat is situated on the edge of the city centre and de Pijp (the Pipe), one of the most popular districts of Amsterdam with lots of small shops, restaurants and bars. Cross the road, and walk through the passage of supermarket Albert Heijn and you're on Albert Cuyp Market. Visit the Heineken experience 150 meters further up the road. You can hop on a canal cruise on the corner of the street. Walk 150 meters further up the road and you're at Rijksmuseum (Rembrandt, van Meer and more Dutch masters of the 17th century), have a snack in the museum garden and enjoy the fountain. Then walk across Museumsquare to van Gogh Museum. Alternatively, cross the bridge and you're in the centre of the city with its beautiful canals and 17th century houses. Of course there are plenty of museums, shops, bars and restaurants to visit there too. Public transport links take you to all parts of Amsterdam within a few minutes. You couldn't be much more central than this spot!

The Riekerpolder is a continuation of the Rietwijkerpolder and the Bovenwegse Sloterpolder (or Sloterbuitenpolder) and was created in 1636 when the area between the Sloterweg and the Nieuwe Meer was diked and drained with a polder mill, the Riekermolen. The polder is part of a peat meadow area that was part of the Hollands-Utrecht peat area.

The pastureland thus created remained intact for centuries. During the reclamation of the Haarlemmermeer (1849-1852), a part of the polder in the southwest was excavated for the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder, between where Badhoevedorp and the hamlet of Nieuwe Meer are now located.

It's easy to find your way in this area!

Most streets in De Pijp are named after Dutch painters, like Jan Steen, Frans Hals, Ruysdael and Vincent van Gogh. Diamantbuurt, Nieuwe Pijp and Oude Pijp are the three districts composing the area.

The busiest street market of the Netherlands, the Albert Cuyp Market, is located in De Pijp. It is open six days per week and attracts tourists. The former Heineken brewery is also a local tourist attraction; the former town hall of Nieuwer-Amstel is one of De Pijp's most notable monuments. name: Glamping lodge Amsterdam city 2
description: Camping among the trees in the middle of the city with the comforts of home. The camping feeling but not the hassle. Sleeping under canvas in a real bed and waking up to the singing of birds and the croaking of frogs. Making a cup of coffee in the kitchenette and enjoying it in the sun on the veranda in front of the tent. By bus or bicycle, you can be in the centre of Amsterdam within 25 minutes. Bikes can be rented at reception and the bus stop is an 8-minute walk away.
neighborhood_overview: What makes it so nice to spend the night at our campsite? Well, that's different for everyone. Some like all the greenery on and around the campsite, others love the fact that you can get to the centre of Amsterdam so quickly. Some can't get enough of the woodpecker sounds or the hooting of an owl, while others can't wait to discover the catering establishments around us. Basically, we are lucky enough to be located in the Tuinen van West, one of Amsterdam's last undiscovered gems, from where you can reach the city centre in no time. description: Our house is located in the Nieuwendam district, a unique green place in the lively Amsterdam North. The house is great for families or a quiet group of friends (28+), who want to relax after a day in the city, and who don't mind occasionally feeding our two lovely cats. neighborhood_overview:
Als je Amsterdam van een kant wil zien die nog niet ontdekt is, moet je naar Amsterdam-Noord komen. Haal je brood op het Purmerplein bij de bakker, of ga lekker dineren bij Lazuur, en wat dacht je van eigengebakken taarten en cacke bij Liever Hier. Allemaal op loop afstand van ons huis.
Of pak de fiets naar Durgerdam, Broek in waterland en Holysloot, waar de tijd lijkt te zijn stil gestaan. Je krijgt een inkijkje in hoe men vroeger woonde. Fiets nog even door langs de boer waar je verse melk en eieren kan kopen en kinderen de kalfjes kunnen knuffelen.
Vanaf ons huis pak je de fiets over de Nieuwerdammerdijk naar het centraal station, wat je 15 minuten kost. Onderweg drink je een biertje bij café Het Sluisje, het oudste café van Amsterdam Noord.
Ons huis wordt omringt door groen; de Schellingewouderbreek met z'n rijke flora en fauna of neem een verfrissende duik in Het IJ bij de Rietlanden.

description:

Located in a quiet street, it is still very close to everything. The Anne Frank house, the beautiful canals, Nine Street shopping area, and many restaurants are within walking distance.

neighborhood_overview:
If you are looking for an authentic Amsterdam neighbourhood, look no further!

Originally a working-class neighbourhood, the Jordaan has become one of the most expensive, upscale locations in the Netherlands. It is home to many art galleries, particularly for modern art, and is also dotted with speciality shops and restaurants. Markets are held regularly at Noordermarkt, the Westerstraat (the Lapjesmarkt textile market) and Lindengracht.

Rembrandt spent the last years of his life in the Jordaan, on the Rozengracht canal. He was buried in the Westerkerk church, at the corner of Rozengracht and Prinsengracht, just beyond the Jordaan. The Anne Frank House, where Anne Frank went into hiding during World War II, is located on the edge of the Jordaan, on the Prinsengracht canal.

Fun fact: The Jordaan is locally seen as the most 'original' place of Amsterdam, still maintaining the typical 'Amsterdam' mentality, inhabitants and atmosphere.

neighborhood_overview: The Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid is part of Plan Zuid by H.P. Berlage. Plan Zuid is divided into several parts: the Apollobuurt and Stadionbuurt, aimed at the wealthy, middle class and working class, and the Rivierenbuurt, aimed at the middle class. The Rivierenbuurt was built in the 1920s and 1930s. The urban plan envisaged that three main streets (Amstellaans) cut through the neighborhood in a Y-shape and converge on Daniël Willinkplein, named after the Dutch writer Daniël Willink (1676-1722). These were the Amstellaan, Noorder Amstellaan and Zuider Amstellaan. The other street names in the area were named after Dutch rivers. Notable exceptions are the Uithoornstraat, which was named after the mooring place on the Amsteldijk of the skipper from Uithoorn, and the Borssenburgplein and street, which were named after a former country estate on the Amsteldijk, which was demolished in 1866.

neighborhood_overview:
Rivierenbuurt is part of the borough of Amsterdam Zuid. It is bordering the Amstel River and features many fine examples of Amsterdam School architecture. It was built in the 1920s as a primarily middle-class residential area, part of the Plan Zuid (Plan South) urban expansion programme designed by famous Dutch architect Berlage. The area mainly consists of fully enclosed apartment blocks, like our house many were designed in the style of the Amsterdam School, characterized by its curvy facades and wealth of fantasy ornaments.

The most striking building in the Rivierenbuurt, and around the corner, is 'De Wolkenkrabber' ('The Skyscraper') at Victorieplein square. The building, which is officially named Twaalf Verdiepingenhuis (Twelve Storey House), was built in 1930-1932 and designed by architect Staal. It was the city's first high residential tower (over 40m high).

The Riekerpolder is a polder in the municipality of Amsterdam, district of Nieuw-West (before 1921 municipality of Sloten), north of the Nieuwe Meer.

The Riekerpolder is a continuation of the Rietwijkerpolder and the Bovenwegse Sloterpolder (or Sloterbuitenpolder) and was created in 1636 when the area between the Sloterweg and the Nieuwe Meer was diked and drained with a polder mill, the Riekermolen. The polder is part of a peat meadow area that was part of the Hollands-Utrecht peat area.

The pastureland thus created remained intact for centuries. During the reclamation of the Haarlemmermeer (1849-1852), a part of the polder in the southwest was excavated for the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder, between where Badhoevedorp and the hamlet of Nieuwe Meer are now located.

The Riekerpolder is a polder in the municipality of Amsterdam, district of Nieuw-West (before 1921 municipality of Sloten), north of the Nieuwe Meer.

The Riekerpolder is a continuation of the Rietwijkerpolder and the Bovenwegse Sloterpolder (or Sloterbuitenpolder) and was created in 1636 when the area between the Sloterweg and the Nieuwe Meer was diked and drained with a polder mill, the Riekermolen. The polder is part of a peat meadow area that was part of the Hollands-Utrecht peat area.

In the house, there was a huge copper boiler or expansion vessel. This ensured that the pressure in the pipes remained at the same level.
